title: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame Commemorative Coin Act
official_summary:
Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame Commemorative Coin Act

(Sec. 3) This bill directs the Department of the Treasury to mint and issue not more than 50,000 $5 coins, 400,000 $1 coins, and 750,000 half-dollar coins in recognition and celebration of the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame.

The coins shall be in the shape of a dome, and the design on the common reverse of the coins shall depict a basketball. Treasury shall hold a competition to determine the design of the common obverse of the coins, which shall be emblematic of the game of basketball.

(Sec. 7) The bill requires all sales of such coins to include specified surcharges, which shall be paid by Treasury to the Hall to fund an endowment for increased operations and educational programming.

summary.headline: A 2018 law lets the Treasury Department mint commemorative coins honoring the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, with sales surcharges going to the Hall.
summary.what_it_does: The Treasury Department must mint and issue up to 50,000 $5 coins, 400,000 $1 coins, and 750,000 half-dollar coins to honor the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. The coins are dome-shaped and show a basketball on the reverse side. Treasury will hold a design competition for the obverse, which must reflect the game of basketball. Every coin sale must include a set surcharge, and Treasury pays those surcharges to the Hall to fund an endowment for its operations and education programs.

who_it_affects.how: People who buy these commemorative coins pay the coin price plus the required surcharge.

who_it_affects.group: The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame
who_it_affects.how: The Hall receives surcharge money from Treasury to build an endowment for operations and educational programming.

who_it_affects.group: The U.S. Mint and Department of the Treasury
who_it_affects.how: Treasury must run a design competition, mint the coins in the set quantities, and pay the surcharges to the Hall.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a specific effective date; the act was enacted on December 21, 2018.
